evidence.title: Pacific nations insist world must increase efforts to meet global warming limit

occurrences.checkable_against: official COP31 host and presidency records
occurrences.quote_span: Turkey is hosting COP31 in the coastal city of Antalya and Australia is leading the negotiations.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Fiji pre-COP31 ministerial climate negotiations

occurrences.checkable_against: official Pacific nations negotiating priorities and UN global temperature projections
occurrences.quote_span: Among those priorities are securing better access to climate finance, protecting oceans, and making sure the target of limiting warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels is honoured, despite projections from the UN that it will soon be exceeded.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Fiji pre-COP31 ministerial climate negotiations

occurrences.checkable_against: COP31 agenda and outcomes, and Chris Bowen's statement
occurrences.quote_span: The pre-COP events in Fiji and Tuvalu this week will shape what is possible at COP31, said Australian climate minister Chris Bowen.
occurrences.speaker: Chris Bowen
occurrences.subject: Fiji pre-COP31 ministerial climate negotiations

occurrences.checkable_against: official agenda and participant records for the Fiji ministerial meeting and COP31
occurrences.quote_span: Pacific nations, which are among the world's most vulnerable to climate change, are trying to lock their priorities into global climate negotiations at the ministerial meeting in Fiji, a precursor to the COP31 forum in Turkey in November.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Fiji pre-COP31 ministerial climate negotiations

occurrences.checkable_against: official transcript or attendance records of the Fiji pre-COP ministerial negotiations
occurrences.quote_span: "We are hurtling past the 1.5-degree temperature limit," Fijian climate minister Lynda Tabuya told representatives from more than 50 countries at the start of pre-COP ministerial negotiations.
occurrences.speaker: Lynda Tabuya
occurrences.subject: Fiji pre-COP31 ministerial climate negotiations

occurrences.checkable_against: Lynda Tabuya's official remarks and Pacific relocation records
occurrences.quote_span: The data simply confirm what Pacific nations can see, she said: "The tide that reaches our homes, the pale reef our grandmothers no longer recognise, the villages we have already had to relocate."
occurrences.speaker: Lynda Tabuya
occurrences.subject: Fiji pre-COP31 ministerial climate negotiations

occurrences.checkable_against: COP21 Paris Agreement adoption records and Chris Bowen's statement
occurrences.quote_span: "This region is home to some of the world's strongest climate voices," he said, adding that Pacific advocacy was vital in the adoption of the 1.5 degree goal at COP21 in Paris in 2015. "It's also experiencing the most direct impacts."
occurrences.speaker: Chris Bowen
occurrences.subject: Fiji pre-COP31 ministerial climate negotiations

occurrences.checkable_against: UN Environment Programme climate assessment cited by Dechen Tsering
occurrences.quote_span: "Pacific risks will outlast the temperature peak," she said. "Each additional 100 years above 1.5 degrees would commit the world to around 40 centimetres (15.8 inches) of additional median sea level rise by 2300 compared with the pathway without overshoot."
occurrences.speaker: Dechen Tsering
occurrences.subject: Fiji pre-COP31 ministerial climate negotiations

occurrences.checkable_against: Murat Kurum's statement and official COP31 summit records
occurrences.quote_span: Turkey's environment minister Murat Kurum, who is president of COP31, said limiting overshoot of the target was the summit's clear common goal.
occurrences.speaker: Murat Kurum
occurrences.subject: Fiji pre-COP31 ministerial climate negotiations

occurrences.checkable_against: official statements and proceedings of the Fiji pre-COP31 ministerial climate negotiations
occurrences.quote_span: Global governments must increase efforts to reduce emissions because the planet is "hurtling past" a critical temperature target that would restrain sea level rises and extreme weather, delegates at a major climate conference in Fiji said on Wednesday.
occurrences.speaker: delegates at a major climate conference in Fiji
occurrences.subject: Fiji pre-COP31 ministerial climate negotiations

occurrences.checkable_against: Murat Kurum's official remarks
occurrences.quote_span: "I believe in this wholeheartedly," he said.
occurrences.speaker: Murat Kurum
occurrences.subject: Fiji pre-COP31 ministerial climate negotiations

occurrences.checkable_against: official transcript of Lynda Tabuya's opening remarks
occurrences.quote_span: "Overshoot (of the target) is not a verdict we accept quietly ... keeping 1.5 alive is the primary legal obligation and duty we are here to uphold."
occurrences.speaker: Lynda Tabuya
occurrences.subject: Fiji pre-COP31 ministerial climate negotiations

occurrences.checkable_against: Dechen Tsering's statement and UN Environment Programme climate assessments
occurrences.quote_span: Exceeding a 1.5-degree rise — and significant environmental damage — was now unavoidable, said Dechen Tsering, director of the Regional Office of Asia Pacific at the UN Environment Programme.
occurrences.speaker: Dechen Tsering
occurrences.subject: Fiji pre-COP31 ministerial climate negotiations
